title: Twenty Drivers and One Phone Line: Gojek's Years Before the App
conflicts: Founding year: 2010 (Gojek, TechCrunch 2019, CNA/INSEAD's Jason Davis, Wikipedia) against 2011 (Jakarta Post 2015 interview, VIVA) and 2009 (Wikipedia lead); story uses 2010, attributed to the company. App launch: January 2015 (Jakarta Post Dec 2015, Gojek) against a March 2014 relaunch (Jakarta Post June 2015) and 2014 (Davis); story uses January 2015. Transport rules: four wheels (Davis) against at least three wheels (ministry via Jakarta Post); story uses the ministry. Driver counts of 600 to 10,000+ in 2015 are Makarim's own and attributed; Wikipedia's uncited 450 drivers in 2012 not used.
notes: Funding set to 'unknown' rather than the slate's 'bootstrapped': no source says how the call-centre years were paid for (first reported outside round late 2014). The edition tells only the 2010-2015 episode and does not mention Makarim's later ministerial career or the Chromebook procurement case; for the editor's awareness, Wikipedia (citing AP, Straits Times and Indonesian outlets) reports he was named a suspect in September 2025 and that a Jakarta court convicted him on 30 June 2026, a verdict he said he would appeal.
